parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour proposes a new Border Security Command with counter-terrorism style powers to tackle criminal smuggling gangs, additional caseworkers to clear the asylum backlog, a new returns and enforcement unit, and negotiating returns agreements with safe countries. The party also commits to linking immigration and skills policy to reduce net migration and end over-reliance on overseas workers.

citations.quote: We will create a new Border Security Command, with hundreds of new investigators, intelligence officers, and cross-border police officers.

Labour will reduce net migration. We will reform the points-based immigration system so that it is fair and properly managed, with appropriate restrictions on visas, and by linking immigration and skills policy.

results.headline: Labour pledges swift, firm and fair asylum system
results.quote: Labour will restore order to the asylum system so that it operates swiftly, firmly, and fairly; and the rules are properly enforced.

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservatives propose a binding legal cap on migration set on work and family visas, falling each year of the next Parliament, alongside continuing removals to Rwanda to deter illegal channel crossings. They also commit to processing all asylum claims within six months and ending the use of asylum hotels.

citations.quote: We will introduce a binding, legal cap on migration, set on work and family visas so public services are protected whilst we bring the skills our businesses and the NHS needs.
We will run a relentless, continual process of permanently removing illegal migrants to Rwanda with a regular rhythm of flights every month, starting this July, until the boats are stopped.

results.headline: Conservatives pledge legal migration cap to guarantee falling numbers
results.quote: Introduce a legal cap on migration to guarantee that numbers will fall every year, so public services are protected while bringing in the skills we need.

results.headline: Conservative MP credits ETA scheme as Conservative border reform
results.quote: The ETA scheme was introduced by the Conservative Government to secure and modernise Britain's borders.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrats propose scrapping the Rwanda scheme and the Illegal Migration Act, ending the Hostile Environment, and replacing the arbitrary salary threshold for work visas with a flexible merit-based system. They also commit to tackling the asylum backlog with a dedicated unit and a three-month service standard for processing claims.

citations.quote: Scrap the Conservatives' Illegal Migration Act and their Rwanda scheme, uphold the Refugee Convention, and provide safe and legal routes to sanctuary for refugees, helping to prevent dangerous Channel crossings.

Replace the Conservatives' arbitrary salary threshold with a more flexible merit-based system for work visas, with the relevant department working with employers in each sector to address specific needs as part of a long-term workforce strategy that also focuses on education and training to address skills gaps from within the UK.

results.headline: Lib Dems pledge to scrap Rwanda scheme and uphold Refugee Convention
results.quote: Scrap the Conservatives' Illegal Migration Act and their Rwanda scheme, uphold the Refugee Convention, and provide safe and legal routes to sanctuary for refugees.

parties.name: SNP
parties.summary: The SNP calls for the devolution of immigration powers to Scotland to create a bespoke migration system addressing Scotland's specific demographic and economic needs, and supports a rural visa pilot scheme to mitigate labour shortages. The party also demands the scrapping of the Rwanda scheme and opposes hostile immigration policies.

citations.quote: Devolve powers to create a bespoke migration system for Scotland that values those who decide to work, live, study and invest here and allows us to address our specific demographic and economic needs.

Introduce a rural visa pilot scheme. Scotland should have full powers over immigration, including the devolution of overseas workers' employment visas. Until then, it is vital the UK Government acknowledges the distinct demographic challenges we face in Scotland and introduce a pilot to mitigate against labour shortages as a result of a hard Brexit and hostile immigration policies.

results.headline: SNP demands devolved bespoke migration system for Scotland
results.quote: Devolve powers to create a bespoke migration system for Scotland.
